versions.short: The bill would revoke a 1964 public land order covering certain federal land and transfer jurisdiction over that land to the Secretary of the Interior. It would then require the Secretary, within 180 days of enactment and subject to valid existing rights, to place about 80 acres of Bureau of Land Management land and about 185 acres of Indian Creek Ranch land into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians. Before that deadline the Secretary would review whether a survey is needed and, if so, perform it and make minor corrections to correct clerical, typographical, and surveying errors, with the survey kept available for public inspection at the Bureau of Indian Affairs. The transferred land would be declared part of the Tribe's reservation and administered under the laws generally applicable to trust property for tribes. The bill would also prohibit using the transferred land for class II or class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.
